audience.text: Python developers building document processing workflows who need to convert or generate PS/EPS/XPS content without relying on Ghostscript or Adobe tooling.

capabilities.text: Read and parse PS/EPS documents using PsDocument.from_file() or from_bytes(), with full PostScript interpretation and DSC/EPS metadata extraction.
capabilities.title: Read and parse PS/EPS documents

capabilities.text: Read XPS packages using XpsDocument.from_file() or from_bytes(), supporting fixed pages and print tickets.
capabilities.title: Read XPS packages

capabilities.text: Create and edit PS/EPS and XPS documents from scratch using PsDocument.create() or XpsDocument.create() with drawing APIs.
capabilities.title: Author PS/EPS and XPS documents

capabilities.text: Write PDF 1.4 output with PdfWriter, including TrueType/Type1 font embedding via FontResolver and FontCache.
capabilities.title: Convert to PDF

capabilities.text: Rasterize PS/EPS and XPS content to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or TIFF using RasterRenderer with Skia or pure-Python fallback for PS/EPS.
capabilities.title: Rasterize to image formats

capabilities.text: Exposes ps_to_pdf, ps_to_image, xps_to_pdf, xps_to_image, and eps_metadata as MCP tools via create_server() for automation.
capabilities.title: Expose conversions as MCP tools

limitations.text: No PDF import or parsing API is provided; the library only writes PDF, it does not read existing PDF files.
XPS-to-image conversion always requires the skia-python backend and has no pure-Python fallback.
Importing aspose.page.pdf.writer or aspose.page.image.raster_renderer before aspose.page.ps raises a circular-import ImportError.
Font embedding requires explicit additional_fonts_folder paths via FontResolver; automatic system-font discovery is not provided.
The MCP server exposes only conversion/metadata tools; document creation APIs like PsDocument.create() are not available as MCP tools.

problems_solved.text: Enables PS/EPS/XPS to PDF conversion without external dependencies like Ghostscript.
Supports rasterization of PS/EPS and XPS content to PNG, JPEG, BMP, and TIFF using the skia-python backend.
Provides programmatic page construction via RenderModelBuilder for generating PDF content from scratch.
Exposes document conversions as MCP tools for LLM-agent and automation workflows.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Page FOSS for Python is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed Python library for reading, authoring, and converting PostScript, EPS, and XPS documents to PDF or raster formats.

uncertainties: Whether the library supports JPEG, BMP, or TIFF output formats beyond PNG is not explicitly confirmed by the provided examples.
The exact behavior of the fallback pure-Python rasterizer for PS/EPS when skia-python is unavailable is not detailed beyond its existence.

workflows.name: PS to PDF conversion
workflows.text: Convert a PostScript file to PDF using the ps_to_pdf MCP handler or PsDocument.to_pdf().

workflows.name: EPS metadata extraction
workflows.text: Extract bounding box and title metadata from EPS files using eps_metadata.

workflows.name: XPS to PDF conversion
workflows.text: Convert an XPS file to PDF using the xps_to_pdf MCP handler or XpsDocument.to_pdf().

workflows.name: Rasterization of PS/EPS to PNG
workflows.text: Render PS or EPS content to PNG using PsDocument.to_image() or RasterRenderer.

workflows.name: Rasterization of XPS to PNG
workflows.text: Render XPS content to PNG using XpsDocument.to_image() or RasterRenderer, requiring skia-python.

workflows.name: PDF generation from render model
workflows.text: Build a PDF directly from programmatically constructed page content using RenderModelBuilder and PdfWriter.
